newsitem.title: FRANCE: INSTANT VIEW-French intervention rate cut.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW-French intervention rate cut.

text.p: Following are analysts' comments on the announcement by the Bank of France on Thursday that it would cut the intervention rate to 3.20 percent from 3.25 percent.
Fifteen of 20 economists polled on Tuesday by Reuters said the central Bank had a "window of opportunity" to ease but the cut was smaller than the 10 basis points many had forecast.
JEAN-LOUIS MOURIER, ECONOMIST, LOUIS DREYFUS FINANCE:
"The bank is continuing to narrow the gap with the German repo rate while remaining prudent. I think they have shown that they remain pragmatic and are watching how things evolve in the markets."
"It was expected. It leaves a margin of manoeuvre for later. They can do the same thing next month to narrow against the German repo. They can (narrow) go as far as 10 basis points.

"The five basis point cut in the intervention rate by the Bank of France is not surprising. The central bank wants to give two messages. On one hand, the franc is gaining so that it can allow a cut in its floor rate. At the same time, it wants to show that it has not changed its monetary policy, in keeping a small spread against Germany."
PAUL HORNE, INTERNATIONAL ECONOMIST, SMITH BARNEY.

"They're taking advantage of their leeway and they need to with unemployment at 12.6 percent. When the French cut interest rates it helps them deal with a basic problem, stimulating growth and creating jobs." He said more rate cuts were probably on the way. "There is 75 percent chance of more rate cuts."

"I was expecting five basis points. There is no domestic or international reason for the Bank to stop cutting interest rates. It is moving with caution, but I think that in five basis point steps, it can bring the intervention rate to parity with the German repo rate."

"The fall is small. But it can be explained by the fact that there is a long holiday weekend ahead (starting on Friday in France). Tomorrow is the (U.S.) employment report which is the main focus of the markets."
She said the cut was "a signal that there will be further falls".
